incidents.optimization: bitsandbytes NF4 4-bit weight quantization
incidents.complaint_verbatim: [Bug]: BitsAndBytes quantization is not working as expected
incidents.complaint_normalized: The bitsandbytes NF4 checkpoint generated punctuation-only output in vLLM while the same base model generated normally through Transformers.
incidents.baseline: Same base model loaded with Transformers load_in_4bit
incidents.resolution: --enforce-eager bypassed the failing path for reported reproductions; no universal backend fix was linked.

incidents.optimization: 50% 2:4 pruning plus channel-wise GPTQ W4A16 through Marlin 2:4
incidents.complaint_verbatim: The model output is abnormal when I use 2:4 sparsity
incidents.complaint_normalized: A valid sparse-and-quantized checkpoint generated corrupted text only when dispatched through the Marlin 2:4 CUDA kernel.
incidents.baseline: The same stage_sparsity checkpoint before the Marlin 2:4 execution path
incidents.resolution: vLLM PR #10464 fixed the Marlin 2:4 CUDA-kernel path; the reporter attributed normal output to that change.

incidents.optimization: compressed-tensors 2:4 sparsity plus dynamic FP8; INT8 also reported, through CUTLASS scaled sparse matmul
incidents.complaint_normalized: The selected CUTLASS sparse-plus-quantized kernel crashed during vLLM engine profiling, preventing model startup.
incidents.baseline: Later vLLM master using the same model recipe
incidents.resolution: Recompiling against a later vLLM master fixed the crash for the reporter.

incidents.optimization: PyTorch 2:4 semi-structured BF16/FP16 sparse linear at a 3072x10240 decode shape
incidents.complaint_verbatim: torch.sparse.to_sparse_semi_structured significantly worsens performance on H100 GPUs
incidents.complaint_normalized: A nominally accelerated 2:4 sparse linear was slower than the dense operation at representative LLM decode dimensions.
incidents.baseline: Dense BF16/FP16 torch.nn.Linear at the same shape

incidents.optimization: GPTQ-Marlin and AWQ W4A16 weight quantization
incidents.complaint_verbatim: Quantization does not lead to Throughput Speedup (Please Help)
incidents.complaint_normalized: W4A16 quantization delivered only about 15% more output throughput than dense inference on the reported short-prompt workload.
incidents.baseline: Dense FP16 vLLM path, with model-metadata differences noted as a confound

incidents.optimization: GPTQ-Marlin weight quantization; AWQ control
incidents.complaint_verbatim: [BUG]: Different quality responses using GPTQ / marlin kernels on A10 vs A100 GPUs
incidents.complaint_normalized: GPTQ-Marlin generated normal prose on one Ampere topology but repetitive nonsense under two-GPU tensor parallelism.
incidents.hardware: one A100 or H100 good path; two A10 GPUs bad path; two RTX 3090 GPUs fix witness
incidents.baseline: AWQ on both topologies and GPTQ-Marlin on one A100/H100
incidents.resolution: A linked vLLM fix restored correct output; another user confirmed it on two RTX 3090 GPUs.

incidents.optimization: q8_0 key/value KV-cache quantization with quantized model weights
incidents.complaint_verbatim: gibberish right away in the first message
incidents.complaint_normalized: Quantized KV state corrupted output after long generation or conversation reuse, while fresh or unquantized-cache runs stayed normal.
incidents.runtime: llama.cpp build 8783; official CUDA Docker reproduction
incidents.baseline: Restart before the final message or disable KV-cache quantization

incidents.optimization: vLLM bitsandbytes and GGUF quantization backends
incidents.complaint_normalized: Maintainers found the backends costly to maintain, weakly used, slower than alternatives, and missing important loader and tensor-parallel features.
incidents.runtime: vLLM backend state described in RFC #39583
incidents.hardware: consumer GPUs and tensor-parallel deployments discussed without one controlled hardware lane
incidents.baseline: Native vLLM quantization backends and llama.cpp GGUF serving

incidents.optimization: Q5 GGUF through KoboldCpp versus GPTQ
incidents.complaint_normalized: The Q5 GGUF variant felt substantially better but too slow, while GPTQ was fast enough but subjectively worse.
incidents.runtime: KoboldCpp for GGUF; GPTQ runtime not reported
incidents.baseline: Q5 GGUF versus GPTQ of the same named model family

incidents.optimization: GGUF Q4_K_M and Q5_K_M weight quantization
incidents.complaint_verbatim: Has anyone tested how quantization hits different capabilities separately? My results are surprising.
incidents.complaint_normalized: Q4 reportedly preserved chat and knowledge scores while causing a much larger multi-step math regression that Q5 nearly removed.
incidents.baseline: FP16 and Q5_K_M on the same unnamed 27B model

incidents.optimization: Q5-to-Q4 weight-quantization reduction
incidents.complaint_verbatim: completely tanks coherence on longer outputs
incidents.complaint_normalized: Some model/quant combinations showed little short-output change but crossed a sharp coherence cliff during long generation at Q4.
incidents.baseline: Q5 variant of the same model

incidents.optimization: whole-layer pruning from 70B to 42B
incidents.complaint_normalized: Near-baseline MMLU did not establish that layer pruning preserved rare languages, specific knowledge, or emergent capabilities.
incidents.baseline: Unpruned Llama-3 70B on five-shot MMLU

incidents.optimization: FP8, GPTQ-INT8, AWQ-INT4, GPTQ-INT4, and BNB-NF4 quantization
incidents.complaint_normalized: Four-bit methods lost up to 59% on long-context tasks despite much smaller average losses at eight bits.
incidents.baseline: Unquantized model checkpoints across 9.7K matched examples
incidents.resolution: Eight-bit quantization averaged about 0.8% accuracy loss; the paper requires model-, task-, method-, and language-specific evaluation before four-bit deployment.

incidents.optimization: SLQ non-uniform asymmetric post-training weight quantization
incidents.complaint_normalized: Task-level parity below four bits did not preserve the full next-token distribution or trajectory-level agreement.
incidents.baseline: FP16 model distributions and outputs
incidents.resolution: Use Expected Acceptance Rate for the stricter contract; the study required roughly 5-6 bits per parameter on average for distribution-lossless compression.

incidents.optimization: llama.cpp --allow-requantize conversion of already-quantized tensors
incidents.complaint_normalized: Requantizing from a lossy source can compound conversion error and severely reduce model quality.
incidents.baseline: Direct quantization from FP16 or FP32 source weights
incidents.resolution: Quantize from FP16/FP32, use an importance matrix, and retain higher precision for sensitive output, embedding, and multimodal tensors.

incidents.optimization: GGUF K-quants from Q2_K through Q8_0
incidents.complaint_normalized: Perplexity degradation rose nonlinearly below Q4/Q5 in the historical quantizer comparison.
incidents.runtime: llama.cpp historical quantizer and perplexity evaluation
incidents.baseline: FP16 perplexity
incidents.resolution: Use higher-bit K-quants when the measured low-bit perplexity penalty violates the workload tolerance.

incidents.optimization: approximately 50% unstructured weight sparsity with sparse GPU SpMM
incidents.complaint_normalized: Existing sparse formats and kernels could not beat dense matrix multiplication at quality-preserving moderate sparsity.
incidents.runtime: custom three-layer sparse format and hybrid tensor-core/CUDA-core kernel
incidents.hardware: modern HBM-equipped GPUs evaluated in the paper
incidents.baseline: Dense GPU matrix multiplication and prior sparse SpMM kernels
incidents.resolution: The paper's specialized representation and hybrid kernel reported up to 1.41x end-to-end speedup over FlashLLM.

incidents.optimization: Q4_K weight quantization plus multi-token prediction under multi-user multi-GPU serving
incidents.complaint_verbatim: Q4 k is minimum you can go, multi user mtp across gpus doesn't work in llama.cpp
incidents.complaint_normalized: The reply asserted both a Q4 quality floor and an MTP failure under concurrent multi-GPU llama.cpp serving.

incidents.optimization: Q2_K weight quantization plus q4_1 key/value KV-cache quantization at 131072-token context
incidents.complaint_verbatim: I was getting nonsense output and on this commit it works fine.
incidents.complaint_normalized: DeepSeek V4 quantized CSA/HCA cache tensors omitted the required Hadamard rotation and produced nonsense output.
incidents.baseline: Same Q2_K model and q4_1 KV-cache recipe on the patched commit
incidents.resolution: llama.cpp PR #25202 applied the required Hadamard rotation to quantized DeepSeek V4 cache paths; a reviewer reproduced the fix.

incidents.optimization: Q4_0 weights with Q5_K_M, IQ4_XS, and UD-IQ3_XXS controls from multiple providers
incidents.complaint_normalized: Several quantized files produced malformed code locally while the API and a different local model behaved normally.
incidents.hardware: RTX 3060 12GB, 64GB system RAM, 45 CPU-offloaded MoE layers
incidents.baseline: Hosted API and GPT-OSS-120B in the same local installation

incidents.optimization: 2-3 bit GGUF weight quantization with shared prefix-cache reuse
incidents.complaint_verbatim: garbled tool calls like <|DSML|tool_callsaplied>, infinite reasoning loops
incidents.complaint_normalized: Low-bit tool-call corruption repeated deterministically under a shared prefix and was rescued by a nonce that forced cache-busting prefill.
incidents.baseline: Retry with a nonce exchange that breaks the shared prefix cache
incidents.resolution: A cache-busting nonce reportedly rescued 18 of 18 corrupted calls, but no root-cause runtime fix was established.

incidents.model: DeepSeek V4 Flash 284B; K160 REAP-pruned 180B variant
incidents.optimization: K160 REAP pruning at 3.99 bpw versus unpruned UD-IQ2_M at 2.56 bpw
incidents.complaint_verbatim: K160 lost non-english completely, English is ok.
incidents.complaint_normalized: The pruned model matched the extreme quant on English agent scenarios but reportedly lost non-English capability completely.
incidents.runtime: llama.cpp deployment described in the source thread
incidents.baseline: Unpruned DeepSeek V4 Flash UD-IQ2_M at the same 90GB memory footprint

incidents.optimization: regular Int8 matrix multiplication versus LLM.int8 mixed-precision decomposition
incidents.complaint_normalized: Regular Int8 scaling failed after a few systematic activation dimensions emerged at model scale.
incidents.hardware: consumer GPU inference evaluated by the paper
incidents.baseline: FP16 checkpoints and regular Int8 quantization
incidents.resolution: Decompose the outlier feature dimensions into a 16-bit matmul while keeping more than 99.9% of values in Int8.

incidents.model: OPT-1.3B and OPT-13B failure examples; broader LLaMA-family evaluation
incidents.optimization: INT3 group-size-128 round-to-nearest versus activation-aware weight quantization protecting 1% salient channels
incidents.complaint_normalized: Naive three-bit group quantization caused catastrophic perplexity, while activation-selected channel protection recovered near-FP16 quality.
incidents.hardware: desktop and mobile GPUs evaluated in the paper
incidents.baseline: FP16 and naive INT3 group-size-128 round-to-nearest
incidents.resolution: Protect 1% of channels selected by activation magnitude using AWQ per-channel scaling.

incidents.model: LLaMA 7B/13B/30B, Llama-2 7B/13B, Mistral-7B, OLMo-1B/7B, and Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct
incidents.optimization: single-weight pruning and round-to-nearest weight/activation quantization with super-outlier preservation
incidents.complaint_normalized: Removing one early-layer super weight collapsed generation and zero-shot accuracy despite leaving billions of other parameters intact.
incidents.baseline: Original FP16 models and naive round-to-nearest quantization
incidents.resolution: Identify and preserve the super weights and induced super activations at high precision.
